# age_encrypted (Resource)

Encrypts `plaintext` to one or more age recipients.

age encryption is randomized, so this is a resource rather than a function or data source: the ciphertext is produced once and kept in state, and only re-encrypted when `plaintext` or `recipients` change. Re-encrypting the same plaintext to a new recipient is how an identity is rotated.

~> **Note:** `plaintext` is stored in state. Use encrypted state or a backend you trust with secrets.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Wrap a random data-encryption key with an age identity, the way tools such
# as Klio (CloudNativePG backups) expect their encryption key file.
resource "random_bytes" "data_key" {
  length = 32

  # Every ciphertext ever produced with this key needs it to decrypt.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "age_identity" "backup" {}

resource "age_encrypted" "data_key" {
  plaintext  = random_bytes.data_key.hex
  recipients = [age_identity.backup.recipient]
}

# Rotating the identity (`tofu apply -replace=age_identity.backup`) re-encrypts
# the same data key to the new recipient; the data key itself never changes.
output "encrypted_data_key" {
  value = age_encrypted.data_key.ciphertext
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `plaintext` (String, Sensitive) The data to encrypt. Changing it re-encrypts.
- `recipients` (List of String) age recipients, X25519 (`age1...`) or post-quantum (`age1pq1...`). Any of the matching identities can decrypt. The two kinds can't be mixed in one list. Changing the list re-encrypts.

### Read-Only

- `ciphertext` (String) The ciphertext, ASCII-armored (`-----BEGIN AGE ENCRYPTED FILE-----`). Multi-line.
- `ciphertext_base64` (String) The binary ciphertext, base64-encoded on a single line. Useful for stores that don't preserve newlines.
- `id` (String) SHA-256 of the binary ciphertext.
